article_text:
Cette année, le Salon Photo & Vidéo se tiendra du 8 au 11 octobre à la grande halle de La Villette. Il s’intéressera autant à l’image animée qu’aux évolutions technologiques et artistiques du médium au cours de ces deux siècles passés.

En 2026, le Salon de la Photo change de nom et devient le Salon Photo & Vidéo. Dans son communiqué, l’événement explique ce changement par l’intérêt croissant pour ce second médium : « Aujourd’hui, la vidéo s’impose comme un langage universel et créatif. De nouveaux acteurs se sont installés sur le marché, des formats innovants apparaissent chaque jour, et les créateurs multiplient les expériences immersives. Qu’il s’agisse de vlog, de courts-métrages, de contenus pour les réseaux sociaux ou de projets artistiques ambitieux, la vidéo est désormais incontournable pour tous les passionnés d’image. » Du 8 au 11 octobre, les visiteurs pourront découvrir 114 exposants et 180 marques, ainsi que des expositions dont certaines feront la part belle à la vidéo. À cela s’ajoutent différentes rencontres avec des réalisateurs, des vidéastes et des créateurs de contenu qui témoigneront de leur approche créative. Ces quatre jours seront également rythmés par des ateliers, des lectures de portfolio et des conférences.

À l’occasion du Bicentenaire de la Photographie , la Grande Exposition du salon s’intéressera aux évolutions technologiques et artistiques du médium. Intitulée Deux siècles d’appareils photographiques (1826-2026) et organisée en partenariat avec le musée Nicéphore Niépce, elle proposera un parcours culturel et pédagogique. Vous pourrez y découvrir une collection unique de boîtiers, allant des débuts de la photographie à nos jours, de même que des tirages d’époque ou des reproductions. Différents procédés seront à l’honneur. Parmi eux se comptent l’héliographie, le daguerréotype, le calotype, le collodion, l’ambrotype ou encore le ferrotype. Ce projet inédit a par ailleurs été labellisé par le ministère de la Culture.

Une conférence, une chasse au trésor et d’autres surprises signées Fisheye

Comme chaque année, les équipes de Fisheye seront présentes sur place et vous proposeront notamment une conférence sur le livre photo à l’heure des réseaux sociaux. Celle-ci aura lieu le vendredi 9 octobre, de 18h à 18h30, et sera animée par Théo Gosselin et Boby . Ce dernier organisera également une chasse au trésor, en partenariat avec Sandisk™, dans la grande halle de La Villette. Au total, vingt enveloppes seront cachées. Toutes vous feront remporter un produit Sandisk™ et cinq d’entre elles, les Gold, vous permettront d’obtenir un exemplaire de Croisette 3000 , de Boby, à sa sortie. Tous les lots seront à récupérer à notre stand. Enfin, grâce à notre code promo FSEYE26, vous pourrez avoir des billets d’entrée gratuits au Salon Photo & Vidéo. Nous vous y attendons nombreux !

article_text:
Announcement

Skirball Cultural Center presents “The 1960s — A Generation on Fire: Judy Baca’s Great Wall of Los Angeles”

The exhibition shares two new sections of the public art mural on view for the first time, featuring moments from an era of collective action that still resonates today.

Great Wall of Los Angeles mural. Courtesy of the artist Judy Baca and the SPARC Archives.

One of California’s most culturally significant landmarks comes to the Skirball with the opening of The 1960s — A Generation on Fire: Judy Baca's Great Wall of Los Angeles featuring new, monumental murals that approach history as a living, contested, and shared narrative in which we all take part.

In 1974, Judy Baca conceived of the Great Wall as a monument to the people of California, featuring a visual history of ethnic peoples from prehistoric times to the 1950s. Soon after in 1976, Baca co-founded the Social and Public Art Resource Center (SPARC) and together with 400 young people working alongside artists, historians, and community members, collaborated to paint the first section of the half-mile mural on the LA River. Since then, Baca and SPARC have been working to extend the mural beyond the 1950s to present day.

Within this exhibition, viewers can observe how the decade was shaped by the moral courage, peaceful protests, and cultural awakening of the Civil Rights Movement and the “generation on fire” who led the way. Visitors will also see recently completed mural sections focused on the 1960s that will soon be added to the existing mural.

The murals are presented alongside preparatory drawings and color studies; an immersive video installation that brings visitors to the banks of the LA River at the Tujunga Wash, the ultimate site for the murals; as well as an interactive component called MuralMemoirs where visitors can share their own histories.

The 1960s — A Generation on Fire: Judy Baca’s Great Wall of Los Angeles is on view at the Skirball, where individual sections will be revealed throughout the exhibition run from October to December 2026 and January to February 2027.

Learn more at skirball.org .

article_text:
David Fincher cut roughly 60 pages from Quentin Tarantino ‘s original screenplay for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” the upcoming “Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood” follow-up starring Brad Pitt.

“The first draft I read was 230 pages. It was essentially two movies,” Fincher told Empire in a new joint interview with Tarantino. The film, which sees Pitt reprise his Oscar-winning role as Hollywood stuntman Cliff Booth, ultimately came in at approximately two hours and 20 minutes.

Related Stories

‘Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir’ Sets Global Season 7 Rollout on Disney, TF1 and Globo

Fincher explained that his interest in the project centered less on its plot than on the opportunity to explore the characters and their relationships against the backdrop of 1970s Hollywood. “I liked the idea that it’s a story around a bonfire,” Fincher said. “It wasn’t about the plot as much as it was about how the participants collided with one another in the back alleys of Hollywood in 1977.”

Tarantino handed over directing duties to Fincher after deciding against making the project himself. Tarantino had previously considered the film as a possible follow-up to his 2019 hit but ultimately decided he did not want a sequel to serve as his 10th and potentially final movie.

Pitt, who previously worked with Fincher on “Se7en,” “Fight Club” and “The Curious Case of Benjamin Button,” helped bring the director onto the project.

Fincher also discussed the process of adapting Tarantino’s screenplay while balancing the creative interests of its writer and star.

“Somewhere in there was the Venn diagram of what Brad wanted to do, what I want to do, what Quentin wanted to do,” Fincher said. “Not ‘want to do,’ but the areas we would focus on.”

Set in 1977, eight years after the events of “Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood,” the new film follows Booth as he takes on work as a Hollywood fixer. While the original film centered on Booth’s relationship with fading television actor Rick Dalton, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, the sequel draws more heavily from crime fiction, including the work of novelist Elmore Leonard, whose book “Rum Punch” served as the basis for his 1997 film “Jackie Brown.”

“I don’t think of it as a hangout movie at all,” Tarantino told Empire. “‘ Once Upon A Time In Hollywood ’ was a hangout movie, but you know you’re going to Cielo Drive [site of the Manson murders]. It has this force, thus I didn’t need a lot of plot. This script was very different…To me, it had the flavor of an Elmore Leonard paperback: a crime-story paperback feel.”

The project reunites Pitt with the character that earned him the Academy Award for best supporting actor in 2020. “Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood,” which also starred DiCaprio and Margot Robbie, received 10 Oscar nominations, including best picture and best director.

“The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is scheduled for an exclusive two-week global IMAX run beginning Nov. 25 before premiering on Netflix Dec. 23.

article_text:
Films and events

Laugh

The Banning Curse

Nefrin-e Toghif

Iranian director Mohsen Amiryousefi discusses his eventful career with the Angel of Death in this hilarious cinematic autofiction about the highs and lows of radical filmmaking.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Mohsen Amiryousefi

With Mohsen Amiryousefi

Iran 2026. 88min

Courtesy of Irimage

Language Persian With English subtitles

Introduction

After the critical success of his first film at Cannes, Amiryousefi returned to Iran to find it banned by state authorities. It’s a pattern that continued through his entire career, which the seasoned director looks back on in this imaginative, satirical portrait. A balance of biography and constructed fiction, the filmmaker’s own life and Iran’s turbulent political, social and cultural history is entwined via a rich trove of archive footage.

Wema Mumma

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lali

Two emotionally scarred strangers are thrust into an arranged marriage, in this wildly original, pitch-black comedy with hints of the supernatural.

In a Whisper

When a young queer woman returns home to Tunisia to mourn her uncle’s death, she finds his cause of death shrouded in mystery.

Hot Water

This atmospheric and sharply funny road movie sees a Lebanese mother and her American son take a trip, with a lot to unpack along the way.

article_text:
Dan Lin has been dismissed as Netflix ‘s head of film after almost three years, multiple sources tell Variety .

Even if expected, it’s a significant shoe to drop following a layoff bloodbath last week at the streamer. Roughly 1,000 employees got the chop, capped by the shock firing of chief content officer Bela Bajaria. Lin was let go at the start of the weekend, two sources added, and will address his teams throughout the day on Monday. The executive attended Saturday’s Academy Gala, and was spotted Sunday evening at a tastemaker screening for “La Bola Negra” on the Netflix campus.

Related Stories

Meghan Markle to Co-Host 'Junior MasterChef Australia'

Meghan Markle 'Deeply Distressed' by Allegations Her Father Possessed Child Sex Abuse Images

A Netflix spokesperson had no immediate comment on the matter. It’s unclear who will replace Lin, though an announcement is expected in the coming days. Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy, the former heads of the Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, have been widely speculated to be speaking with the streamer about a possible role at the company.

Netflix is embarking on a major creative restructuring after months of headlines citing engagement problems and stock stagnation — all in the aftermath of its defeated bid for Warner Bros. — namely in hiring the seasoned film and TV executive Peter Rice to replace Bajaria. In the days leading up to his ouster, Lin watched as layoffs claimed his right hand Doug Belgrad and the film vertical’s indie head Sheroum Kim.

Lin’s ascension to the top Netflix film job turned heads in 2024. The accomplished producer sat atop a thriving self-made business in Rideback. That production house is best known for building the animated “Lego” film franchise, Stephen King’s “It” adaptations and the “Sherlock Holmes” movies.

He departed Rideback to replace longtime film lead Scott Stuber. In a June sit-down with The New York Times, Lin said that he greenlit or acquired 88 movies for Netflix up to that point, with the standouts being “Apex,” “Emelia Perez,” “Here Comes the Flood” and “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”

Jack Dunn contributed to this post.

article_text:
Aus Sicherheitsgründen schließt die Art Basel Paris früher als geplant. Was sich besonders gelohnt hat, lesen Sie hier. Und einige der Nebenmessen bleiben auch am Wochenende geöffnet

Eva Presenhuber auf der Art Basel Paris

Im Erdgeschoss des Grand Palais bei den big shots kann es schon mal etwas einförmig werden, denn hier zeigen alle, was gut und teuer ist und möglichst bald im Sales-Report auftauchen soll. Da wirkt der Stand von Eva Presenhuber sehr erfrischend. Der Künstler Ugo Rondinone hat ihn kuratiert und Werke von Künstlerinnen und Künstlern der Galerie in Petersburger Hängung an die Wände gebracht. Hier finden sich Zeichnungen, Drucke und Originale von Dieter Roth, Franz West, Trisha Donnelly, Sarah Hughes und vielen anderen. Und in der Mitte: eine massive Skulptur von Rondinone selbst.

Eva Presenhuber , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, B37

Sieh dir diesen Beitrag auf Instagram an Ein Beitrag geteilt von Galerie Eva Presenhuber (@galerieevapresenhuber)

Fortes D'Aloia & Gabriel auf der Art Basel Paris

Organisch, nah am Körper – das sind die Werke bei der brasilianischen Galerie Fortes D’Aloia & Gabriel. Schon aus den späten 90er-Jahren stammt die große, rosafarbene, geraffte Leinwand von Leda Catunda mit ihrer abstrakten Körperlichkeit. Ernesto Netos spinnenhaft-abstrakte Stahlskulptur tritt in einen Dialog mit seiner transparenten, schlangenartigen Wandskulptur aus gewebten Fäden, und die Malerei von Marina Rheingantz entführt in eine abstrakte Landschaft.

Fortes D'Aloia & Gabriel , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, B48

ChertLüdde und Ellen de Bruijne Projects auf der Art Basel Paris

Ein aus Stoffen gefertigtes Tor mit Blumen und Schlingpflanzen markiert den Eingang des Gemeinschaftsstands von ChertLüdde und Ellen de Bruijne Projects. Dahinter leuchtet ein weicher, wulstiger Kussmund in Rot, den man sich an die Wand hängen kann: Pauline Curnier Jardins Installation fällt auf – und bildet einen schönen Dialog mit den Textilcollagen der 2016 verstorbenen Clemen Parrocchetti, die auf weibliche Körperteile anspielen. Komplettiert wird die subversive Feier der Weiblichkeit durch die wirklich lustigen Textgemälde von Lily van der Stokker. "Men, playing football, ruling the world, cute", steht da zum Beispiel in hübsch verschlungener Poesiealbum-Schrift. Das macht sich in jedem Haushalt gut.

ChertLüdde und Ellen de Bruijne Projects , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, K3

Maxwell Graham auf der Art Basel Paris

Zwei Flaschen hängen hektisch zitternd an Fäden von der Decke, angeschlossen an Elektrokabel. Drinnen vibriert jeweils ein klapperndes braunes Etwas. Der Wandtext informiert: Es sind Kniescheiben. Eine ähnlich lakonische Härte hat die Fotografie von Zoe Leonard, die eine Fassade mit zugemauerten Fenstern zeigt. Der minimalistische Stand von Maxwell Graham aus New York wirkt wie ein Schlag ins Gesicht.

Maxwell Graham , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, L6

Sieh dir diesen Beitrag auf Instagram an Ein Beitrag geteilt von Maxwell Graham Gallery (@maxwellgrahamgallery)

Karma International auf der Art Basel Paris

Eine phallische, schillernde Rakete von Sylvie Fleury weist den Weg zum Stand von Karma International, deren Cast von Künstlerinnen verschiedener Generationen konstant exzellent ist. Hier trifft eine Fotografie der jüngst verstorbenen Künstlerin Valie Export auf eine absurde Tortenskulptur von Gina Fischli, und ein Paillettenbild von Pamela Rosenkranz glitzert. Die melancholisch-existenzielle Malerei der jungen Ukrainerin Kateryna Lysovenko findet ein angemessenes Gegenüber in der schweren Körperlichkeit der Skulptur des Quotenmanns im Ensemble, Hans Josephsohn.

Karma International , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, L20

Plan B auf der Art Basel Paris

Bei der Galerie Plan B dreht sich alles um Mythen und Legenden, und neben den Galeriestars Adrian Ghenie und Ciprian Mureșan fällt hier die 1995 geborene Tincuta Marin auf. Sie beschäftigt sich mit antiken Bildwelten, zitiert ägyptische Mythologien und überführt sie in ihren großformatigen, mit Reliefs kombinierten Malereien in eine sehr zeitgenössische Form – zurück zur Antike!

Galeria Plan B , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, L21

Eli Kerr auf der Art Basel Paris

Zu ihrem Debüt auf der Art Basel Paris präsentiert die Montrealer Galerie Eli Kerr eine ambitionierte Installation von Rosario Aninat und Simon Shim-Sutcliffe, die sich während ihres Studiums an der Städelschule in Frankfurt am Main kennenlernten und seitdem eng zusammenarbeiten. Sie zeigen eine stufenförmige Konstruktion aus dunklem Holz mit Objekten, die zeitlos wirken und zwischen Skulptur und Gebrauchsgegenstand schweben – wie eine Sammlung von Werkzeugen, deren Zweck in Vergessenheit geraten ist.

Diese aus Stein, Glas, Gips, Metall und Holz gefertigten Relikte des Modernismus – etwa ein Turm aus perforiertem Metall oder ein flaches, schalenartiges Gefäß – leiten ihre Formen von alten chinesischen Jadeobjekten ab. Eine Einzelausstellung des Duos wird am 3. Dezember 2026 in der Kunsthalle Mannheim eröffnen.

Eli Kerr , Art Basel Paris im Grand Palais, M24

Cosima von Bonin im Petit Palais

Im Petit Palais lagern Meerestiere auf Podesten: Tintenfische und Delfine breiten ihre schlaffen Glieder aus und sehen dabei extrem putzig aus. Dazu kommen Muscheln mit Kulleraugen, die der Muppet Show entsprungen zu sein scheinen. Cosima von Bonin hat diese Tierchen aus Leder und Samt für die Präsentation der Herbst-/Winterkollektion von Loewe geschaffen, jetzt haben sie den Laufsteg für sich allein. Die Präsentation ist Teil des Public Programs der Art Basel Paris, das sich auf der Straße zwischen Grand Palais und Petit Palais mit Werken von Yinka Shonibare, Alicja Kwade, Manfred Pernice und anderen fortsetzt – und heute leider aus Angst vor Vandalismus vorzeitig abgebaut wird .

Public Program: Cosima von Bonin " Dollys & Beaux" , präsentiert von Petzel , Gaga und Neu , Art Basel Paris im Petit Palais

Corpus auf der Paris Internationale

Der schottische Künstler Richard Walker nutzt Licht und Schatten, um vertraute Räume zu verfremden. Seine Ölgemälde auf Holzplatten oszillieren dabei zwischen Gegenständlichkeit und Abstraktion. Oft lässt er sich von seiner Atelierumgebung inspirieren und arbeitet in zwei Maßstäben: Größere Werke setzt er in mühevoller Handarbeit aus einzeln bemalten Sperrholzfragmenten zusammen, inspiriert vom japanischen Holzschnitt. Vier Werke sind auch noch am Wochenende auf der Paris Internationale zu sehen, ausgestellt bei Corpus, einer 2025 in Cambridge gegründeten Galerie, die zum ersten Mal bei der jungen Pariser Nebenmesse dabei ist. Erfreulich, dass eine junge britische Galerie hier über Londons Tellerrand hinausschaut.

Corpus , Paris Internationale , 1 87-189 Quai de Valmy, B3

Sieh dir diesen Beitrag auf Instagram an Ein Beitrag geteilt von CORPUS (@corpusgallery_)

Cooper Cole auf der Post-Fair

Auf der Post-Fair, die zum ersten Mal in Paris stattfindet (und auch am Wochenende noch offen ist), zeigt die Galerie Cooper Cole aus Toronto eine klar fokussierte Zweierausstellung der indigenen Métis- Künstlerin Gabrielle L’Hirondelle Hill und der kanadischen Künstlerin Jenine Marsh, die beide alltäglichen Materialien eine unerwartete Bedeutung und Monumentalität verleihen.

Hills "Spells", eine seit 2018 fortlaufende Serie, die bereits im MoMA ausgestellt wurde, besteht aus Zeichnungen, die mit tabakgetränktem Fett überzogen sind und auf die wirtschaftliche und politische Geschichte des Tabaks sowie dessen Rolle in indigenen Tauschsystemen verweisen. Marshs konservierte Gänseblümchen, die von batteriebetriebenen LEDs beleuchtet werden, halten Schönheit und Verfall sowie Künstlichkeit und Natur in einem unbehaglichen Gleichgewicht.

Cooper Cole , Post-Fair , Rue du Temple, 004

For the past two weeks, Film

Comment

has been reporting from the picturesque shores of the Lido di Venezia, where the Venice Film Festival takes place each year.

For our final Podcast from this year’s edition, which wrapped over the weekend,

Film Comment

Co-Editor Devika Girish invited critics Mariona Borrull, Leonardo Goi, Luke Hicks, and Öykü Sofuoğlu to discuss three late-festival premieres: Ali Asgari’s

A Bit of Light

(4:30); Casey Affleck’s

Company

(8:42); and Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s

NAZA

(15:25). The group closed things out by shouting out their personal highlights from this year’s Venice.

title_original: Akinola Davies Jr. on My Father’s Shadow
editorial_title_zh: Akinola Davies Jr. 谈《我父亲的影子》
editorial_excerpt_zh: 家庭肖像：导演谈论他这部省略、氛围感十足的处女作剧情片，故事设定在1993年的尼日利亚
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "故事设定在1993年的尼日利亚，Akinola Davies Jr. 这部省略、氛围感十足的《我父亲的影子》是一幅处于政治危机边缘的国家肖像。我们通过影片年轻主人公的眼睛经历这些事件——两个男孩在拉各斯与父亲共度一天。他们为能与常常缺席的老爸度过一段美好时光而兴奋不已——但他们也感觉到周围正酝酿着麻烦，即便他们并不明白所有细节。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《电影评论》编辑Devika Girish与Davies交谈，他刚凭这部影片赢得英国电影学院奖最佳处女作奖，谈及他在与兄弟Wale共同撰写剧本时在多大程度上借鉴了家庭记忆；剧组如何重现1990年代尼日利亚的质感、声音与感觉；以及为什么将儿童视角置于这个故事的核心很重要。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Set in Nigeria in 1993, Akinola Davies Jr.’s elliptical, atmospheric My Father’s Shadow is a portrait of a country on the cusp of a political crisis. We experience these events through the eyes of the film’s young protagonists, two boys who spend a day in Lagos with their father. They’re thrilled at the prospect of some quality time with their often-absent old man—but they also sense that there’s trouble brewing around them, even if they don’t understand all the details."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Film Commen t Editor Devika Girish spoke with Davies, who just won a BAFTA for Outstanding Debut for the film, about the extent to which he drew upon family memories while writing the script with his brother, Wale; how the crew recreated the textures, sounds, and feel of 1990s Nigeria; and why it was important to have a children’s perspective at the heart of this story."}]
article_text:
Set in Nigeria in 1993, Akinola Davies Jr.’s elliptical, atmospheric My Father’s Shadow is a portrait of a country on the cusp of a political crisis. We experience these events through the eyes of the film’s young protagonists, two boys who spend a day in Lagos with their father. They’re thrilled at the prospect of some quality time with their often-absent old man—but they also sense that there’s trouble brewing around them, even if they don’t understand all the details.

Film Commen t Editor Devika Girish spoke with Davies, who just won a BAFTA for Outstanding Debut for the film, about the extent to which he drew upon family memories while writing the script with his brother, Wale; how the crew recreated the textures, sounds, and feel of 1990s Nigeria; and why it was important to have a children’s perspective at the heart of this story.

人気ゲーム『ペルソナ』シリーズ30周年を記念した大規模展覧会「PERSONA 30th EX.」が2027年1月21日から2月7日まで上野の森美術館（東京）で開催されます。 2027年発売予定の『ペルソナ4 リバイバル』を含むシリーズ作品のアートや立体造形、本展初公開の制作資料の展示など、シリーズの奥深い魅力を余すことなく体感できる展覧会です。（美術展ナビ編集班）

『ペルソナ』シリーズとは 第1作『女神異聞録ペルソナ』から2026年で30周年を迎える『ペルソナ』シリーズ。 日本の街を舞台に学校生活や友情、恋愛などの身近な日常を体験しながら、同時に噂話や都市伝説などオカルティックな非日常に立ち向かっていくジュブナイルRPG。「ペルソナ」とは自分の中に眠るもうひとりの自分が、伝来の神や悪魔の姿となって出現したもの。心の力に目覚めた少年少女たちが出会い、幾多の困難に抗い、成長していく物語が描かれる。

PERSONA 30th EX.

article_text:
The Róng Museum of Art and founding director Pi Li have appointed Freya Chou, Li Jia, and Susanna Zhu as curators ahead of the institution’s slated opening in the second half of 2027.

Currently under construction as a private venture of Ma Huateng, the founder of technology company Tencent, the museum will focus on the visual culture of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. The 53-metres-high, the 4,500-square-metre institution has been designed by Büro Ole Scheeren.

Chou and Li Jia will oversee the museum’s research, exhibitions, and public programs. Recent curatorial projects by Chou include Hong Kong artist Ellen Pau’s first major survey exhibition at SculptureCenter , New York (2026), the 13th Taipei Biennial (2023), and Hong Kong’s participation at the 2022 Venice Biennale.

Li Jia previously served as deputy director of Pace Beijing (2012–2015) and senior curator at Taikang Space (2015–2020).

Susanna Zhu will lead the museum’s learning and public engagement initiatives, moving from the Zishi ESG Garden Community Museum of Sustainability where she was director

article_text:
A news item by ArtThrob Editors on the 19th of October 2026. This should take you 3 minutes to read.

All four independent members resign from Johannesburg Art Gallery Committee, urge end to legal battle as Gallery and collection deteriorate

All four independent, non-governmental members of the Art Gallery Committee of the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG) have resigned. They say a years-long dispute between the City of Johannesburg and the Friends of the Johannesburg Art Gallery, joined by the Johannesburg Heritage Foundation, has displaced urgent work on the Gallery. Meanwhile its building is in disrepair and one of the continent’s most significant public art collections is housed in conditions that compromise its physical integrity. Their statement and the correspondence behind it are published at www.jagreset.com .

Key facts

Who: Pfunzo Sidogi (member since 2022), Molemo Moiloa (since 2022), Nontobeko Ntombela (since 2018) and Joseph Gaylard (since 2014), the Committee’s four independent members.

What: Resignation from the Art Gallery Committee with FAQs and supporting documents. Also an Open letter that charts a future set of terms and conversations for how to address the foundational issues of the JAG.

Why: The members say the dispute over who has authority over JAG, and over remedial measures and resources, has stalled progress, and that they can no longer make meaningful progress from inside the Committee. They wish to make clear what the key issues to be addressed actually are.

Legal context: The Friends of JAG have applied to the High Court for, among other things, the members’ removal.

Where: www.jagreset.com

“We no longer believe that we can make meaningful progress from inside this structure,” the members said. They say they step down in the hope of replacing a costly and unnecessary legal battle with a process of transparency, honesty and productive conversation.

The Gallery’s situation

The members describe a building in disrepair, a collection at physical risk, and an institution without the capacity, resources or clear direction it needs. They say these problems are urgent but surmountable.

They say the City has not allocated budget to complete the temporary relocation of the collection, has made it hard for external partners to contribute, and has incurred significant legal costs. They say the Friends have driven a public campaign that has misdirected attention from the problems that need solving. In their view, the conflict has also deterred the corporate and private supporters the Gallery now depends on.

The members also criticize the Friends’ general process thus far, and in particular their court application, which asks for the Mayor and two officials to appoint four new independent members within thirty days, with no criteria, nominations, public input or required expertise.

What the documents show

The Open letter includes a set of steps that the former members understand to be the core issues that impact the JAG’s ability to move forward, including a costly and wasteful legal fight, a lack of clarity on governance issues and the need to rethink the structure of the municipal governance model to enable greater functionality of the JAG. This open letter invites members of the public who agree, to support it.

The published material includes the members’ correspondence with the Office of the Mayor from December 2024 and July 2025. It sets out their call for a cooperative framework managed and mediated by neutral parties, and the conditions on which they would return to the Committee. The members reject the account of their conduct in the court papers and say the record contradicts it.

What happens next

The members address their open letter to the Board of the Friends of the Johannesburg Art Gallery, the Johannesburg Heritage Foundation and the Office of the Executive Mayor, setting out what they believe should happen, and have shared this publicly. The public can sign the open letter at jagreset.com.

The members also thanked JAG’s Chief Curator and staff, who they say have held the institution together in conditions no professional should be asked to work in.

article_text:
All’arte contemporanea viene imputato di ridursi, spesso, a mero prodotto finanziario: impiegata costantemente nell’affannosa corsa dietro al trend del momento, piegata al presenzialismo da fiera e all’algoritmo strappalike dei social. Eppure, se si vuole essere del tutto onesti, il rapporto distopico fra arte e sistema economico è sempre esistito: fra i più pregevoli capolavori che ereditiamo dal passato, molti erano soggetti ai voleri di chiese e monarchie che, pagando, indicavano cosa dovesse o non dovesse essere dipinto o scolpito. L’opera di Andrea Fogli , assolutamente contemporanea ma che potrebbe anche provenire da epoche remote, si discosta da tutto questo. Nei suoi lavori c’è un rigore e una fedeltà intellettuale a un sé in quanto artista che raramente si riscontra così in misura così piena, sia nell’arte del passato che in quella del presente.

Non fa eccezione Atlas Partenope , la mostra ospitata al Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte di Napoli, a cura di Vincenzo Stanziola – la seconda esposizione museale napoletana dopo quella del 2023 al Museo Duca di Martina – e che abita alcuni spazi del secondo piano della dimora reale. Una «Galassia immaginale partenopea» – così l’artista ama definire sinteticamente il suo intervento – affidata a uno dei medium da lui preferiti, il carboncino, tratteggia in dieci polittici una genesi caotica e incontrollabile dove sacro e profano si intrecciano e in cui iconografia aulica e rappresentazione di strada trovano un felice connubio.

Andrea Fogli assolve al compito non facile di sfuggire alla retorica del “vedi Napoli e poi muori” grazie a uno sguardo personale che non rifiuta simboli triti ma assolutamente impermeabile alla “captatio benevoletiae”: sui 140 fogli che compongono i dieci polittici del nucleo centrale, capuzzelle e pulcinella si intrecciano a primule e ginestre, Madonne e Sfingi incontrano i femminielli e figure del presepe napoletano.

Merita certamente un’attenzione particolare la tecnica scelta dall’artista per la realizzazione del polittico: i disegni sono infatti realizzati imprimendo il carboncino su carta generalmente destinata all’uso quotidiano “non-artistico” – come la comune carta da alimenti – attraverso un processo calcografico in cui, attraverso la pressione esercitata, il carboncino si trasferisce al substrato poroso o oliato. Il mezzo utilizzato, la carta, e la tecnica scelta, la “stampa” con carboncino, rendono l’opera effimera e particolarmente delicata. In tale scelta si riconosce ancora la necessità di Fogli di rimanere fedele a se stesso e all’idea originaria: non ci sono compromessi, la caducità dell’opera non è un limite ma ne amplifica il senso.

La realtà non è mai univoca, non è mai totalmente definita. La realtà – quella napoletana ancor di più – è mutevole e inafferrabile, quando si crede di averla finalmente raggiunta si scoglie fra le mani, come un sottile pezzo di carta sotto la pioggia.

Ma la ricerca di Andrea Fogli non si esaurisce nel carboncino su carta, anzi. La poliedricità dell’artista si esprime interamente nelle tre sale dell’esposizione di Capodimonte, fra loro concatenate: l’ambiente centrale che raccoglie i disegni dell’Atlas Partenope dialoga con le “ripitture” di santini e cartoline postali realizzati negli ultimi venti anni e con l’inedita installazione in argilla cruda che, quasi come un’epigrafe, segna l’ultimo ambiente della mostra. Il tema della devozione è il fil rouge che lega tutte le opere in mostra in un ciclo, quello di Atlas Partenope , che è solo il primo capitolo di un nuovo Atlante tutto dedicato a questo tema e che si collega ai precedenti sette Atlanti realizzati dall’artista negli ultimi 25 anni.

La mostra Atlas Partenope di Andrea Fogli sarà visitabile fino al 31 gennaio 2027.
excerpt_original: Al Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte, Andrea Fogli presenta Atlas Partenope: 140 disegni per una geografia mutevole e immaginaria di Napoli L'articolo Andrea Fogli, forme fragili per una realtà inafferrabile: la mostra al Museo di Capodimonte proviene da exibart.com .

article_text:
Films and events

Debate

A Good Little Soldier

Un Bon Petit Soldat

Stéphane Brizé’s taut exploration of the dynamics of power in the modern workplace features Alba Rohrwacher and Vincent Lindon at the top of their game.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Stéphane Brizé

Screenwriters Stéphane Brizé, Coralie Amédéo, Olivier Gorce

With Alba Rohrwacher, Vincent Lindon

France 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Gaumont

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Carla is the new head of HR in a large insurance company. Beneath the veneer of positive and inclusive management exists an insidious and crushing reality that will catch her off guard. Executed with chilling precision within enclosed, clinical spaces and propelled by an unnerving jazz score, A Good Little Soldier captivates and unsettles in equal measure.

Laure Bonville

Content advice

Contains ableist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ink

Danny Boyle brings a seismic moment in Rupert Murdoch’s Fleet Street career blazingly to life, employing the breathtaking style of a story torn from the headlines.

Fjord

This searching, Palme d’Or-winning moral dilemma pits preaching conservative Christian parents against a holier-than-thou liberal system.

Heysel 85

This is a gripping and sobering dramatic reconstruction of the tragedy that unfolded during the 1985 European Cup final between Liverpool and Juventus at the Brussels stadium.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 独家：赶在万圣节之际，这是一个契合时机的公司公告。常驻迪拜的独立导演兼编剧费萨尔·哈什米（Faisal Hashmi）正式创立了专注于类型片的制作公司 Spine Drop Pictures，并公布了首批三部恐怖长片片单。哈什米已赢得了……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "独家：赶在万圣节之际，这是一个契合时机的公司公告。", "links": [{"text": "Halloween", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/halloween/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "常驻迪拜的独立导演兼编剧费萨尔·哈什米（Faisal Hashmi）正式创立了专注于类型片的制作公司 Spine Drop Pictures，并公布了首批三部恐怖长片片单。", "links": [{"text": "Faisal Hashmi", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/faisal-hashmi/"}, {"text": "Spine Drop Pictures", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/spine-drop-pictures/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在为期15年的职业生涯中，哈什米凭借10部场景集中、高概念且带有惊悚反转的类型短片积累了众多粉丝，其中包括《Amber》、《Wicken》和《Skipped》等，这些短片曾在许多电影节上放映，并在YouTube上获得了超过300万的总播放量。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Hoba2.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Dark Sky Films获得获奖阿联酋恐怖片《The Vile》的美国版权", "links": [{"text": "Dark Sky Films Takes U.S. Rights To Prize-Winning Emirati Horror 'The Vile'", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/10/dark-sky-films-us-rights-emirati-horror-vile-1237144216/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/GettyImages-2194140713-1.jpg?w=300", "alt": "2025年1月迪拜天际线照片", "caption": "", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "迪拜电影节将于2027年12月回归，而沙特阿拉伯红海电影节2026年举办情况尚不确定", "links": [{"text": "Dubai Film Festival To Return In December 2027, As 2026 Edition Of Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Film Festival Looks Uncertain", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/09/dubai-film-festival-return-saudi-red-sea-film-uncertain-1237106423/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了导演工作外，他最近还担任了阿联酋导演阿里·F·穆斯塔法（Ali F. Mostafa）备受期待的长片《City of Life Continuum》的联合编剧，该片是其2009年突破性处女作《City of Life》的续集。", "links": [{"text": "City of Life Continuum ,", "url": "https://deadline.com/2025/03/nour-el-nabawy-lin-yin-amp-kayode-akinyemi-ali-f-mostafa-dubai-set-city-of-life-continuum-1236310261/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "在 Deadline 上观看", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈什米还签约编剧并执导英语时间循环恐怖惊悚片《Fractal》，由杰森·弗莱明（Jason Flemyng）和加布里埃拉·瓦加斯（Gabriela Vargas）主演。该片由维也纳的 Pont Pictures 制作，计划于2027年在塞尔维亚开机拍摄。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈什米对 Spine Drop Pictures 的战略规划是聚焦于高概念、具商业导向的类型片，预算控制在100万美元以下，并借鉴他此前拍摄短片时如何在紧张预算下创作的经验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他向 Deadline 表示：“我一直都在思考，如何在减少取景地和资源的同时讲好一个精彩的故事，并让概念保持足够强大，从而不会让人觉得是在试图用廉价成本去拍一部昂贵的大片，而是拍出一部精简、且从一开始就以最佳方式制作的电影。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "首批片单涵盖《Off Plan》、《Cinder》和《Latching》，均由哈什米编剧并执导。", "links": [{"text": "Latching", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/latching/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Off Plan》是一部互相关联的恐怖选集电影，由六个故事组成，在短短一个夜晚的时间里在迪拜展开。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈什米设计了一种模块化的拍摄方法，使得这六个部分可以作为独立的短片作品进行拍摄，并能够独立安排档期，从而通过共享剧组和制作资源获得更大的灵活性和成本效益。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Cinder》被称为一部坚韧的超自然惊悚片，故事背景设定在阿联酋严酷偏远的山区地貌中。该片改编自哈什米于2020年荣获大奖的短片《Amber》，在该短片中，阿联酋偏远公路小镇的一名理发师发现自己正在对抗一名绑架了年轻女孩的残忍绑匪。该短片曾斩获阿联酋艾因电影节最佳影片奖。", "links": [{"text": "UAE", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/uae/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈什米将《Latching》描述为一部女权主义附身复仇恐怖片，故事在巴基斯坦卡拉奇一个惊心动魄的夜晚展开，目前正在当地开发制作。长期居住在阿联酋的哈什米拥有巴基斯坦血统。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈什米在谈到其战略时继续表示：“我们已经从《Obsession》、《Undertone》和《Good Boy》等低成本、高概念恐怖片的国际成功中看到了各种可能性。在阿联酋这样新兴的独立电影市场中，我认为这种方法尤为重要。我们需要那些不仅具有创作雄心、而且具备商业可行性、并拥有现实盈利潜力和国际吸引力的电影。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“一个可持续发展的电影产业并不是靠资助一部昂贵的电影建立起来的。它是靠制作能够找到观众、收回投资并帮助资助下一部作品的电影建立起来的。这就是 Spine Drop Pictures 背后的思考。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈什米表示，随着首批长片的推进，Spine Drop Pictures 正在探索片单投资、国际合拍、战略融资和发行合作的机会。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Here’s a nicely timed company announcement for Halloween .

Dubai-based indie director and writer Faisal Hashmi has officially launched genre-focused production company Spine Drop Pictures and unveiled its inaugural slate of three horror features.

Hashmi has won fans over his 15-year career with a collection of 10 contained, high-concept genre shorts with chilling twists, including as Amber , Wicken and Skipped , which have screened at scores of film festivals and generated more than three million combined views on YouTube.

Related Stories

Dark Sky Films Takes U.S. Rights To Prize-Winning Emirati Horror 'The Vile'

Dubai Film Festival To Return In December 2027, As 2026 Edition Of Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Film Festival Looks Uncertain

Alongside directing, he also recently took co-writing credits on Emirati director Ali F. Mostafa’s long-awaited feature City of Life Continuum , a sequel to his breakout 2009 debut City of Life .

Watch on Deadline

Hashmi is also attached to write and direct English-language, time-loop horror-thriller Fractal , starring Jason Flemyng and Gabriela Vargas, which is being produced by Vienna-based Pont Pictures and is targeting a 2027 shoot in Serbia.

Hashmi’s strategy for Spine Drop Pictures is to focus on high concept, commercially oriented genre pictures, budgeted at below $1 million and tapping into his experience of working on a tight budget with his short films.

“I’ve always looked at how can I tell an amazing story with less locations, fewer resources, but still make the concept so strong that it doesn’t feel like I’m trying to make an expensive movie for cheap, but rather a movie that feels contained and is made in the best way to make it in the first place,” he told Deadline.

The inaugural slate spans Off Plan , Cinde r and Latching , which have been written and will be directed by Hashmi.

Off Plan is an interconnected horror anthology featuring six stories unfolding across Dubai over the course of a single night.

Hashmi has designed a modular shooting approach so that the six segments can be filmed as separate short-form productions that can be scheduled independently, allowing for greater flexibility and cost efficiency through shared crew and production resources.

Cinder is billed as a gritty supernatural thriller set against the unforgiving remote mountain landscapes of the UAE . It expands on Hashmi’s award-winning 2020 short film Amber, in which a barber in a remote UAE highway town finds himself up against a vicious kidnapper who has abducted a young girl. The short won best film at the UAE’s Al Ain Film Festival.

Hashmi describes Latching as a feminist possession-revenge horror film unfolding over the course of a single harrowing night in Karachi, Pakistan, where it is being developed for production. Longtime UAE resident Hashmi is of Pakistani descent.

“We’ve seen what’s possible internationally with the success of low-budget, high-concept horror films like Obsession , Undertone and Good Boy . In an emerging independent film market like the UAE, I think that approach is especially important. We need films that aren’t just creatively ambitious, but commercially viable, with a realistic potential for profitability and international appeal,” continued Hashmi on his strategy.

“A sustainable film industry isn’t built on getting one expensive film financed. It’s built on making films that can find audiences, recover their investments and help finance the next one. That’s the thinking behind Spine Drop Pictures.”

Hashimi says Spine Drop Pictures is exploring opportunities for slate investment, international co-productions, strategic financing and distribution partnerships as it advances its inaugural features.

東北6県の美術館・博物館など 文化の秋にちょっとオトクな文化体験！ そんなキャッチフレーズで10月31日と11月1日、「 東北文化の日 」が展開されます。秋も深まる東北を楽しむチャンスです。日付のない場合は10月31日、11月1日が無料です。代わりに「文化の日」の11月3日などを無料にしている施設の情報も後段に添えてありますので、ご活用ください。

article_text:
Nearly 40 years after first opening the Lament Configuration on screen, Clive Barker is ready to explore pain and pleasure again in the Hellraiser film franchise.

With the recent release of the Saber Interactive’s Hellraiser: Revival video game, the writer/director of the original 1987 horror movie, which was based on his own book, teased that he has “many ideas” of where to take the franchise next.

“I think what was achieved in the game is a wake-up call to anyone who’s been involved in the making of a franchise like Hellraiser ,” he told Dread Central .

Related Stories

‘Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival’ Video Game Devs On Making The Franchise “Nobly Provocative” In The Modern Age

‘Hellraiser’: Jamie Clayton To Play Pinhead As Spyglass-Hulu Movie Sets Cast, Clive Barker To Produce

“It says to get your ideas warmed over so you can go back into existing worlds in a brand new way,” added Barker. “I have many ideas that I’d like to see realized in the Hellraiser universe, and I’m planning to keep my fingers in that pie.”

Watch on Deadline

Based on his 1986 novella The Hellbound Heart , Barker wrote and directed the first Hellraiser movie the following year, introducing audiences to Pinhead (Doug Bradley) and his Cenobites. The franchise has since sparked 11 movies, multiple books, comics, video games and more.

Barker successfully reclaimed U.S. rights to the Hellraiser franchise in 2020, joining the 2022 David-Bruckner helmed Hulu reboot as a producer.

解説・あらすじ

2020年に起きた「京都ALS患者嘱託殺人事件」に迫ったドキュメンタリー。 2020年7月、ALS（筋萎縮性側索硬化症）を患う女性からの依頼で薬物を投与し殺害したとして、2人の医師が逮捕された。ひとり暮らしの彼女は事件当時は眼球しか動かせず、24時間の介護を必要としていた。主犯の大久保愉一は、女性が“安楽死”を望む言葉を投稿していたSNSで彼女と出会っており、事前に130万円の報酬を受け取り、初対面からわずか15分ほどで殺害を実行した。捜査により過去の殺人事件への関与も浮上するなか、メディアは大久保の過去のブログなどから、彼の生命軽視の姿勢を大々的に報じた。そして2025年、嘱託殺人罪などで懲役18年の刑が確定。救命が第一義とされるはずの医師が、なぜ一線を越えて彼女を手にかけたのか。 監督は、和歌山毒物カレー事件を検証した映画「マミー」の二村真弘。亡くなった女性の父親、SNS上での彼女を知る元看護師や難病当事者、医療とケアの専門家への取材を重ねて彼女の人生を掘り下げていくとともに、大久保の母親やかつての医師仲間のもとを訪ねてその半生をたどる。さらに大久保の供述分析を独自におこない、彼が収監されている大阪拘置所へと向かう。京都出身の俳優・田畑智子が声の出演を務め、亡くなった女性がインターネット上につづった切実な言葉の数々を代読。

article_text:
Interest in Elizabeth Holmes and the Theranos fraud scandal has surged amid buzz for You Can See Everything , the record-breaking documentary on the disgraced former CEO.

Viewership for The Dropout , the 2022 Hulu series starring Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, surged by 186% in September compared with the month prior, according to Variety , after the announcement on 6 September of the previously secret film’s first teaser.

Viewership nearly doubled again during the week of 12 October, increasing 92% over the week prior in the days before the film’s 16 October premiere.

Additionally, Bad Blood, the 2018 book by journalist John Carreyrou detailing the inner workings of Holmes’s fraudulent empire and the whistleblowers who exposed her, returned to the New York Times bestseller list.

Holmes, at one point the youngest female self-made billionaire in the US with a net worth $4.5bn by the time she was 30, left the company in 2018, after Carreyrou’s reporting revealed that she and others knew that Theranos devices could not accurately test blood samples. The company collapsed shortly afterward.

The three-hour film, produced by A24 and directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim , opened to an extraordinary $15m (A$21.5m, £11.2m) in North America on just 855 screens – the best opening weekend for documentary in more than two decades, since Fahrenheit 9/11, in 2004, as well as the best opening for a film playing on fewer than 1,000 screens since Borat opened to $26.5m, in 2006. There were reportedly 2,000 sold-out screenings over the weekend.

The film also pushed the weekend’s champion, the video game adaptation Street Fighter , to second place on Monday’s box office chart.

Filmed largely in secret in 2023, in the month before Holmes submitted to prison for an 11-year sentence for fraud, You Can See Everything has played to sold-out showings on the strength of spoiler-averse word of mouth and near-unanimous rave reviews. It holds a rare close-to-perfect score on Rotten Tomatoes and universal acclaim with a 97 on Metacritic , and is among the highest-rated films all time on Letterboxd. In a five-star review , the Guardian called it “a stupefying and gloriously destabilizing hall of psychological mirrors, a thrilling once-in-a-lifetime collision of director and subject”.

Pundits are also predicting that the film could become the first documentary ever nominated for an Oscar for best picture. Additionally, due to the film’s twisty second half – minor spoilers ahead – A24 will submit You Can See Everything for consideration for cinematography, score, director, costume design, production design, and makeup and hairstyling on top of best documentary.

Variety also confirmed on Tuesday that Amanda Seyfried will be campaigned for best supporting actress.

You Can See Everything will expand to at least 2,600 screens on its second domestic weekend, with many industry eyes on its box office rise. It will premiere in Australia on 12 November and in the UK on 20 November.

translated_title_zh: You Can See Everything Mania 提高了 The Dropout 的观众数量 186%
translated_excerpt_zh: 成功的Elizabeth Holmes纪录片引发了对获奖的关于Hulu的故事系列以及《坏血》(Bad Blood),2018年关于丑闻《陌生人比幻想》的书:Lance Oppenheim如何制作今年最受欢迎的两部电影《你不能做这件事情》。

title_original: 【2026 世界公視大展】在世界爆炸之後，還有無數的爆炸──《被北京盯上》、《走過廣島的千枝子》、《仇恨上線中》
title_zh: 【2026 世界公視大展】在世界爆炸之後，還有無數的爆炸──《被北京盯上》、《走過廣島的千枝子》、《仇恨上線中》
summary_zh: 来源摘录：我們正站在一個全新的世界入口。演算法塑造了我們看見的世界，人工智慧改變了愛與死亡的界線，仇恨與謠言能跨越國界迅速蔓延，而國家權力與科技，也正以前所未有的方式介入我們的記憶、身分與日常生活。這個世界比以往更加便利，也更加複雜；資訊更加自由，真相卻未必更容易抵達。 這篇文章 【2026 世界公視大展】在世界爆炸之後，還有無數的爆炸──《被北京盯上》、《走過廣島的千枝子》、《仇恨上線中》 最早出現於 釀電影 。

"credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《被北京盯上》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "➀《被北京盯上》：你相信這些都是真的嗎？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2018 年，我在北京當了半年的交換學生，與留在臺灣的朋友大談臺獨、政治認同與軍事議題時，我說：「我們這樣用微信通電話，真的可以嗎？」朋友想了一下，說：「我們也不是什麼重要的反抗分子吧？」──後來，我果真沒有發生任何事，平安回到臺灣。再後來，兩岸局勢愈發緊張，中國亦宣布暫停赴臺自由行。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我偶爾會覺得，自己搭上了一輛頭也不回的時代末班車。就在去北京的前一年，2017 年，中國知名異議人士華湧（1969－2022）站在被政府強拆的北京市大興區新建村等地，舉起自拍棒。 華湧的鏡頭畫質完全不夠清晰，但足夠拍出身後廢墟的漫天塵埃，他在鏡頭前說：「我身後的東西好像一陣狂風暴雨。（這是）颱風？地震？都不是──是人為的！」當時的他，正在抗議北京掃除低端人口的不正義。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "這位長年在中國反抗共產黨的藝術家，因為拍了這場強拆建案，致使住所屢遭警察盤查，想找他「談談」。受到關切的華湧，急切地在鏡頭前錄下了一段影片。當年，朋友的調侃不能說是一語成讖，是非常悲傷地切中了事實。那句話的意思是，若你是個真正的異議分子，你的確會時常被監控。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "並非為了「觀眾」所拍的，而是為了他的小女兒，華湧以遺書般的心情，祝福女兒三歲生日快樂。其後，華湧一路逃到泰國、土耳其、巴黎，最後暫時落居加拿大，我們可以在片中得知，至少在泰國與最後的居所加拿大，都有中共派遣的祕密警察「艾瑞克」緊密跟蹤。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了華湧，另一位想必會讓臺灣觀眾驚呼出聲的受訪者，是近日談論臺北市長蔣萬安，而在社群爆紅的張堯。 張堯也是中國反共意見領袖，長年在加拿大殷勤更新影片，而張堯為了不讓危險找上自己，她做得很絕：「（在中國）我沒有任何朋友，極少數人才能找上我，我媽媽是我唯一可以信任的人。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "縱使如此，也不代表張堯無法被攻破。在社群平臺 X（前 Twitter）上有非常多小帳號，四處散布著張堯的換臉裸照、誇張的性醜聞，以及收受美方金援等謠言，甚至連張堯的親友資料，也都被公布到網路上。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "張堯是如何看待華湧之死？她的判斷是：「他很有可能被中國政府殺害。」"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/SMh9Zllv1UjRJWFCFG6nsThuHkJVaMRpuGIaZwVp36E/w:729/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/2bc6cf40-4e13-40d5-a259-b687888e5aca.jpg", "alt": "《被北京盯上》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《被北京盯上》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在 2022 年，華湧在划船出海時，不幸遇溺死亡。以意外結案的華湧之死，真正死因是一團迷霧，但華湧身邊的親友，與曾經監控過他的艾瑞克，都對這場「自然死亡」有不小的疑慮。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《被北京盯上》（In Beijing's Crosshairs，2022）有近似俄羅斯娃娃的結構，觀眾以為在談華湧，其實張堯也很重要。你以為只會談被監控的人，不，其實一直監控著華湧，如今從政治祕密警察反叛的「艾瑞克」也現身鏡頭告訴你，他當年是怎麼追蹤華湧，並騙取他的信任的。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艾瑞克的現身，堪稱本片高潮，他提供了祕密警察如何通信、監控華湧，他又如何寫跟監報告等等的內容。有趣的是，他似乎不怕自己露面，而導演也問起他叛逃後的未來，他說： 「未來的事情確實不太好說，也許以後中國政府會想用某種方式把我處理掉。這也是有可能的，不好說。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "從寫出回憶錄《等待在夜裡被捕》（Waiting to be Arrested at Night，2023）的維吾爾族詩人塔依爾・哈穆特・伊茲格爾（Tahir Hamut Izgil）、知名出版人富察（李延賀），乃至臺灣相聲演員黃逸豪的一場車禍，背後是由中國政府出資指使的跨境鎮壓行動⋯⋯在在證明被北京盯上，不只是盯上而已。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "總有人能超然物外、指點江山地，談論某些異議分子就是因為賺「意識形態財」才翻車──然而，這部片澈底揭露出，這是極權政府對個人的全球性獵捕。那麼，還要發生多少事情，我們才願意相信這些都是真的？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「被北京盯上」片名的真正含意，在於它似乎永遠是行動中的未完成式──被盯上以後，我們會怎麼樣？這種鬼影幢幢、無限靠近的危機，才是讓人最為驚悚的身體記憶。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/E_yjhBT5TX8k428GB8tj7GgPkFvn1w6BZRC_IsI6138/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/a9a41e01-3400-4920-a732-52862d6c4c31.png", "alt": "《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "➁《走過廣島的千枝子》：繼續活下去是可以的吧？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「原爆的時候，我十五歲。」 ──走過歷史現場的老者切明千枝子（Chieko Kiriake）這麼說時，語氣十分雲淡風輕。我瞬間想起最近流行的網頁遊戲《八十億分之一》。在進入遊戲以前，玩家沒能選擇太多設定，就會被拋擲進任何一個時代。在玩這款遊戲的時候，我們或多或少會感覺到，我也太無能為力了。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大多數時候的玩家作為一個小小的個體，根本無法「超脫」過於龐大的歷史事件（比如你可能玩到柏林圍牆倒塌、或是罹患某個沒有解藥的流行病）。在遊戲進行時，會讓玩家歷經長大的每一歲，並標示出這一年的世界發生了什麼事、妳／你又發生了什麼事，來讓玩家做出人生、成長與財富的關鍵決定。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《走過廣島的千枝子》（Life and Death, Dreams and Illusions：Kiriake Chieko’s 95 Years，2025）的故事卻不只是模擬人生，千枝子在 15 歲遇到了原爆。雲淡風輕的背後，具備多重的複雜意涵：一者是她時常在鏡頭裡的喟嘆，走過七、八十個年頭以後，千枝子經常會思考，這個災難是真的嗎？她偶爾會感到錯覺，以為整段人生只是一個比較大的幻覺罷了。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我們能夠從千枝子充滿活力卻恍然的側臉中，窺見這位年近百歲的老者，對於自己所背負的歷史，有時是多麼想要「遺忘」。但，作為走過原爆的活歷史，千枝子又豈能真的當作什麼事都沒有發生？於是，她又必須回頭打撈那些生命裡驚駭的「血之碎片」──原子彈投下的時候，強光閃過。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/eCWs1qSq6bJwxxnKba1BKzAry1eJooOGs5rSgs3lfzo/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/308b3b73-2c2b-4a89-8134-7af5b572d6a5.png", "alt": "《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "再回神，千枝子看到全身起水泡的同學，踉蹌地朝她走來。她跟老師提著烹飪課用的油、塗在大家的傷口上，但大家一個一個斷了氣；她跟老師拖著死者（學妹們）的遺體到挖好的坑、協助火化逝者的肉身，目睹人的身體就在火裡壯盛燃燒，發出啪滋啪滋的聲音，自己無法克制地感到驚駭與發抖。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一次又一次，千枝子走進教室、講堂，一再述說那些在廣島的兒時見聞。她打開日曆，上面全塞滿了某時某地的通告記號，以免自己忘記。 站上臺，她反覆提起這些回憶，但不訴諸情緒。每一次的陳述，回憶都不再私密，而是面向世界的提醒，千枝子的生命不再只代表自己──此時此刻，她會站在這裡，是軍國主義造就的悲劇，與其燃燒的灰燼。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了本身因吸收輻射而略顯年輕的容貌之外，她的人生也面臨著是否要生育的困境。千枝子與其伴侶無法確定是否要生小孩，萬一生出「小頭病」的孩子該怎麼辦？醫師提醒他們的念頭，有歧視身心障礙之嫌。最終，他們成功生下健康的孩子，孩子也生出自己的孩子⋯⋯走過數十個年頭，這個與死神擦身而過的女人，如今是家族裡最古老的核心。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她沒有僅止於含飴弄孫，而是不斷前往各種地方：梳化、更衣、佝僂著身體，不將自己澈底封閉。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/1IxmYcvEr5hmOezLcTlDcJ8NRl8sfQEwG2G7aVf_85A/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/8b06136c-530f-4fc8-9feb-fad3677cf8c7.png", "alt": "《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「原爆的前一天，應該跟平常沒什麼不同吧？」晚飯時，她的兒子問。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「我們聽了工作分配，最後猜拳決定誰要做那份工作。⋯⋯最後，猜輸的那班，全部都沒能逃過一劫。那場猜拳決定了我們的命運。」千枝子答道。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "觀看《走過廣島的千枝子》，有時會不意將千枝子的模樣與電影《群山淡景》（A Pale View of Hills，2025）的演員廣瀨鈴相互對照，於是觀者也會恍然：這是從小說總走出來的人物嗎？可惜不是。是後者走進了前者的歷史，而前者還在努力向未來的人訴說：我們要記得，千萬不要回到過去。我們要記住死去的人。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "臨末，電視放映著原爆 80 周年的紀念會現場直播，千枝子閉上雙眼，沉默地雙手合十。出門時，她套上一件西裝外套，拄著傘，朝遠方快步而行；兒子趕在她身後，腳步還有點趕不上媽媽。 「即便他們的身軀早已消逝，但我始終將他們的回憶珍藏在心中，並且會不斷傳承下去。只要這份傳承延續，他們的生命便不會消逝。」──如此觀之，千枝子果然總在趕路。總在路上。她趕著要讓大家繼續活下去。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/QknbZevr8vi-57pe9s-ZTT8nVji3uUChz988LXH6hfQ/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/c77c2a9d-93a2-49a3-b7f3-f433d28ccbee.jpg", "alt": "《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "➂《仇恨上線中》：歧視是如何鍊成的？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "庫德族是世界上未獨立建國的民族中，人口數最繁浩的一群人。他們來自土耳其，後逸散到各地，包含《仇恨上線中》（Kawaguchi and the Kurds：Uncovering the Truth，2025）主要拍攝的日本川口縣。有約莫兩千五百名庫德人落腳在此，於 2024 年左右，他們開始遭到令人不安的對待。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影一開始，蒙面男子舉著手機，對著已經打烊的庫德人烤肉店進行錄影，也不說用途。老闆問：「你為什麼要拍我們的店？」拍攝者說：「為什麼不行？大家都在拍啊。」──事實上，現場四周根本沒人。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "近兩年，日本公廣電視臺 NHK，開始追蹤、調查川口縣的庫德人歧視問題。在社群平臺 X（前 Twitter）上，NHK 團隊找到非常多已被證實是假消息的貼文：庫德族小孩在商店行竊（在短短的錄影中，小女孩只是摸了商品，並沒有帶走）；不知名的人用 AI 製圖，讓一群庫德人舉著「日本人滾出川口」口號（這群人根本沒這麼做過）；也有人拍庫德人遊行，拍到日本庫德族文化協會會長拿著大聲公喊話，語意不清，遂被指責是在吶喊「日本人去死」。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事實上，會長的原句是「去精神病院吧！你們這群種族歧視者！」──這些三分真七分假的攻擊性言論，使得庫德人在網路上的風評急速劣化。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/2FSDmFgAmG3CrAkcGJCbtMZvwnLe-FU42b4a_y1xEeQ/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/718022d9-3cc1-41a1-adb7-3201821dfceb.jpg", "alt": "《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "團隊訪問到其中一位，曾對庫德族發表不當言論的「千佳先生」，千佳在 X 上積極發過不少貼文，包含指稱川口庫德族人和恐怖分子脫離不了關係。起初，他之所以會發文，是因為在職場與庫德族人產生衝突，後來便看所有庫德族人都不順眼。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在影片中，「相對剝奪感」是一個重要的詞彙──當大家看到錯誤的報導，言及庫德人都向日本政府拿補助，每月領有兩千至三千元美金，再加上庫德人的工薪，簡直讓庫德人賺翻了。「如果還不用繳稅，那也太爽了！」推文寫道。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "貼文有三百六十萬次點閱。不過，真正的真相是：這個家庭只領過四個月的補助，而那是距今 13 年前的往事。推文讓許多網友群情激憤，然而令他人感到憤怒的狀況，基本上並不存在。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "是誰扎了稻草人？為什麼要綁一個，沒有任何烏鴉會停留的稻草人？也許，把視線轉移到他者身上，用憤怒驅動自己前進，就能降低自己生活中觸目可見的不順心。唯獨有些火，燒過了頭，放火的人也是會燙到手的。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/qtbFpAUffc982fS2mMilNUorzvrX7wuOPrts3jxWMwY/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/bd6c2b2b-b6c9-4ed9-b0d7-7a7c755b21f8.jpg", "alt": "《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「千佳先生」在日本法院明令禁止仇恨集會時，忽然停止不發文了。他讓自己跟庫德人仇恨言論保持距離，甚至對鏡頭說：「如果真的有人因為庫德人而受到傷害，那他當然可以出來發表評論⋯⋯但現在看起來，是局外人在搧風點火。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "對庫德人的仇恨從川口發生，散布到全國；如今嚇到的人，竟是最初縱火的人。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "歧視是如何鍊成的，臺灣人可一點也不陌生：移花接木的短影片，沒有來由的長文、強渡惡意的立場，戮力曲解某人的言論。要毀掉一個（群）人，首要要讓他們面目可憎，讓眾人產生理由去相信，自己有義務「解決」某個問題，以讓我們的生活「變得更好」。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "──然而，這是真的嗎？我們製造了一個敵人，就真的能使我們的生活安然無恙嗎？又或者只是煉成了歧視？《仇恨上線中》給了警世的思考。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/njcZMxScqvxgbC9Lxaw6zTiDmOkiF3wRAQciMT534X4/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/d72e4fbc-55d1-46a7-ae1e-a1c6741720a7.jpg", "alt": "【2026 世界公視大展】主視覺。／圖像提供：公共電視", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "【2026 世界公視大展】主視覺。／圖像提供：公共電視"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我們正站在一個全新的世界入口。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "演算法塑造了我們看見的世界，人工智慧改變了愛與死亡的界線，仇恨與謠言能跨越國界迅速蔓延，而國家權力與科技，也正以前所未有的方式介入我們的記憶、身分與日常生活。這個世界比以往更加便利，也更加複雜；資訊更加自由，真相卻未必更容易抵達。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "〈美麗新世界〉並非歌頌一個理想未來，而是邀請觀眾重新想像，我們究竟正在走向哪裡。本屆影展共十四部作品橫跨五個單元，從歷史創傷、女性生命、數位科技、媒體操控，到全球政治與極端化現象，帶領我們穿越看似陌生卻早已降臨的現實，在一次次觀看與思辨之中，共同理解這個正在成形的美麗新世界。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "↘【𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 𝘉𝘦𝘴𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘐𝘕𝘗𝘜𝘛 article_text:
撰文／趙鴻祐 劇照提供／公共電視 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

《被北京盯上》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

➀《被北京盯上》：你相信這些都是真的嗎？

2018 年，我在北京當了半年的交換學生，與留在臺灣的朋友大談臺獨、政治認同與軍事議題時，我說：「我們這樣用微信通電話，真的可以嗎？」朋友想了一下，說：「我們也不是什麼重要的反抗分子吧？」──後來，我果真沒有發生任何事，平安回到臺灣。再後來，兩岸局勢愈發緊張，中國亦宣布暫停赴臺自由行。

我偶爾會覺得，自己搭上了一輛頭也不回的時代末班車。就在去北京的前一年，2017 年，中國知名異議人士華湧（1969－2022）站在被政府強拆的北京市大興區新建村等地，舉起自拍棒。 華湧的鏡頭畫質完全不夠清晰，但足夠拍出身後廢墟的漫天塵埃，他在鏡頭前說：「我身後的東西好像一陣狂風暴雨。（這是）颱風？地震？都不是──是人為的！」當時的他，正在抗議北京掃除低端人口的不正義。

這位長年在中國反抗共產黨的藝術家，因為拍了這場強拆建案，致使住所屢遭警察盤查，想找他「談談」。受到關切的華湧，急切地在鏡頭前錄下了一段影片。當年，朋友的調侃不能說是一語成讖，是非常悲傷地切中了事實。那句話的意思是，若你是個真正的異議分子，你的確會時常被監控。

並非為了「觀眾」所拍的，而是為了他的小女兒，華湧以遺書般的心情，祝福女兒三歲生日快樂。其後，華湧一路逃到泰國、土耳其、巴黎，最後暫時落居加拿大，我們可以在片中得知，至少在泰國與最後的居所加拿大，都有中共派遣的祕密警察「艾瑞克」緊密跟蹤。

除了華湧，另一位想必會讓臺灣觀眾驚呼出聲的受訪者，是近日談論臺北市長蔣萬安，而在社群爆紅的張堯。 張堯也是中國反共意見領袖，長年在加拿大殷勤更新影片，而張堯為了不讓危險找上自己，她做得很絕：「（在中國）我沒有任何朋友，極少數人才能找上我，我媽媽是我唯一可以信任的人。」

縱使如此，也不代表張堯無法被攻破。在社群平臺 X（前 Twitter）上有非常多小帳號，四處散布著張堯的換臉裸照、誇張的性醜聞，以及收受美方金援等謠言，甚至連張堯的親友資料，也都被公布到網路上。

張堯是如何看待華湧之死？她的判斷是：「他很有可能被中國政府殺害。」

《被北京盯上》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

在 2022 年，華湧在划船出海時，不幸遇溺死亡。以意外結案的華湧之死，真正死因是一團迷霧，但華湧身邊的親友，與曾經監控過他的艾瑞克，都對這場「自然死亡」有不小的疑慮。

《被北京盯上》（In Beijing's Crosshairs，2022）有近似俄羅斯娃娃的結構，觀眾以為在談華湧，其實張堯也很重要。你以為只會談被監控的人，不，其實一直監控著華湧，如今從政治祕密警察反叛的「艾瑞克」也現身鏡頭告訴你，他當年是怎麼追蹤華湧，並騙取他的信任的。

艾瑞克的現身，堪稱本片高潮，他提供了祕密警察如何通信、監控華湧，他又如何寫跟監報告等等的內容。有趣的是，他似乎不怕自己露面，而導演也問起他叛逃後的未來，他說： 「未來的事情確實不太好說，也許以後中國政府會想用某種方式把我處理掉。這也是有可能的，不好說。」

從寫出回憶錄《等待在夜裡被捕》（Waiting to be Arrested at Night，2023）的維吾爾族詩人塔依爾・哈穆特・伊茲格爾（Tahir Hamut Izgil）、知名出版人富察（李延賀），乃至臺灣相聲演員黃逸豪的一場車禍，背後是由中國政府出資指使的跨境鎮壓行動⋯⋯在在證明被北京盯上，不只是盯上而已。

總有人能超然物外、指點江山地，談論某些異議分子就是因為賺「意識形態財」才翻車──然而，這部片澈底揭露出，這是極權政府對個人的全球性獵捕。那麼，還要發生多少事情，我們才願意相信這些都是真的？

「被北京盯上」片名的真正含意，在於它似乎永遠是行動中的未完成式──被盯上以後，我們會怎麼樣？這種鬼影幢幢、無限靠近的危機，才是讓人最為驚悚的身體記憶。

《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

➁《走過廣島的千枝子》：繼續活下去是可以的吧？

「原爆的時候，我十五歲。」 ──走過歷史現場的老者切明千枝子（Chieko Kiriake）這麼說時，語氣十分雲淡風輕。我瞬間想起最近流行的網頁遊戲《八十億分之一》。在進入遊戲以前，玩家沒能選擇太多設定，就會被拋擲進任何一個時代。在玩這款遊戲的時候，我們或多或少會感覺到，我也太無能為力了。

大多數時候的玩家作為一個小小的個體，根本無法「超脫」過於龐大的歷史事件（比如你可能玩到柏林圍牆倒塌、或是罹患某個沒有解藥的流行病）。在遊戲進行時，會讓玩家歷經長大的每一歲，並標示出這一年的世界發生了什麼事、妳／你又發生了什麼事，來讓玩家做出人生、成長與財富的關鍵決定。

《走過廣島的千枝子》（Life and Death, Dreams and Illusions：Kiriake Chieko’s 95 Years，2025）的故事卻不只是模擬人生，千枝子在 15 歲遇到了原爆。雲淡風輕的背後，具備多重的複雜意涵：一者是她時常在鏡頭裡的喟嘆，走過七、八十個年頭以後，千枝子經常會思考，這個災難是真的嗎？她偶爾會感到錯覺，以為整段人生只是一個比較大的幻覺罷了。

我們能夠從千枝子充滿活力卻恍然的側臉中，窺見這位年近百歲的老者，對於自己所背負的歷史，有時是多麼想要「遺忘」。但，作為走過原爆的活歷史，千枝子又豈能真的當作什麼事都沒有發生？於是，她又必須回頭打撈那些生命裡驚駭的「血之碎片」──原子彈投下的時候，強光閃過。

《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

再回神，千枝子看到全身起水泡的同學，踉蹌地朝她走來。她跟老師提著烹飪課用的油、塗在大家的傷口上，但大家一個一個斷了氣；她跟老師拖著死者（學妹們）的遺體到挖好的坑、協助火化逝者的肉身，目睹人的身體就在火裡壯盛燃燒，發出啪滋啪滋的聲音，自己無法克制地感到驚駭與發抖。

一次又一次，千枝子走進教室、講堂，一再述說那些在廣島的兒時見聞。她打開日曆，上面全塞滿了某時某地的通告記號，以免自己忘記。 站上臺，她反覆提起這些回憶，但不訴諸情緒。每一次的陳述，回憶都不再私密，而是面向世界的提醒，千枝子的生命不再只代表自己──此時此刻，她會站在這裡，是軍國主義造就的悲劇，與其燃燒的灰燼。

除了本身因吸收輻射而略顯年輕的容貌之外，她的人生也面臨著是否要生育的困境。千枝子與其伴侶無法確定是否要生小孩，萬一生出「小頭病」的孩子該怎麼辦？醫師提醒他們的念頭，有歧視身心障礙之嫌。最終，他們成功生下健康的孩子，孩子也生出自己的孩子⋯⋯走過數十個年頭，這個與死神擦身而過的女人，如今是家族裡最古老的核心。

她沒有僅止於含飴弄孫，而是不斷前往各種地方：梳化、更衣、佝僂著身體，不將自己澈底封閉。

《走過廣島的千枝子》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

「原爆的前一天，應該跟平常沒什麼不同吧？」晚飯時，她的兒子問。

「我們聽了工作分配，最後猜拳決定誰要做那份工作。⋯⋯最後，猜輸的那班，全部都沒能逃過一劫。那場猜拳決定了我們的命運。」千枝子答道。

觀看《走過廣島的千枝子》，有時會不意將千枝子的模樣與電影《群山淡景》（A Pale View of Hills，2025）的演員廣瀨鈴相互對照，於是觀者也會恍然：這是從小說總走出來的人物嗎？可惜不是。是後者走進了前者的歷史，而前者還在努力向未來的人訴說：我們要記得，千萬不要回到過去。我們要記住死去的人。

臨末，電視放映著原爆 80 周年的紀念會現場直播，千枝子閉上雙眼，沉默地雙手合十。出門時，她套上一件西裝外套，拄著傘，朝遠方快步而行；兒子趕在她身後，腳步還有點趕不上媽媽。 「即便他們的身軀早已消逝，但我始終將他們的回憶珍藏在心中，並且會不斷傳承下去。只要這份傳承延續，他們的生命便不會消逝。」──如此觀之，千枝子果然總在趕路。總在路上。她趕著要讓大家繼續活下去。

《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

➂《仇恨上線中》：歧視是如何鍊成的？

庫德族是世界上未獨立建國的民族中，人口數最繁浩的一群人。他們來自土耳其，後逸散到各地，包含《仇恨上線中》（Kawaguchi and the Kurds：Uncovering the Truth，2025）主要拍攝的日本川口縣。有約莫兩千五百名庫德人落腳在此，於 2024 年左右，他們開始遭到令人不安的對待。

電影一開始，蒙面男子舉著手機，對著已經打烊的庫德人烤肉店進行錄影，也不說用途。老闆問：「你為什麼要拍我們的店？」拍攝者說：「為什麼不行？大家都在拍啊。」──事實上，現場四周根本沒人。

近兩年，日本公廣電視臺 NHK，開始追蹤、調查川口縣的庫德人歧視問題。在社群平臺 X（前 Twitter）上，NHK 團隊找到非常多已被證實是假消息的貼文：庫德族小孩在商店行竊（在短短的錄影中，小女孩只是摸了商品，並沒有帶走）；不知名的人用 AI 製圖，讓一群庫德人舉著「日本人滾出川口」口號（這群人根本沒這麼做過）；也有人拍庫德人遊行，拍到日本庫德族文化協會會長拿著大聲公喊話，語意不清，遂被指責是在吶喊「日本人去死」。

事實上，會長的原句是「去精神病院吧！你們這群種族歧視者！」──這些三分真七分假的攻擊性言論，使得庫德人在網路上的風評急速劣化。

《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

團隊訪問到其中一位，曾對庫德族發表不當言論的「千佳先生」，千佳在 X 上積極發過不少貼文，包含指稱川口庫德族人和恐怖分子脫離不了關係。起初，他之所以會發文，是因為在職場與庫德族人產生衝突，後來便看所有庫德族人都不順眼。

在影片中，「相對剝奪感」是一個重要的詞彙──當大家看到錯誤的報導，言及庫德人都向日本政府拿補助，每月領有兩千至三千元美金，再加上庫德人的工薪，簡直讓庫德人賺翻了。「如果還不用繳稅，那也太爽了！」推文寫道。

貼文有三百六十萬次點閱。不過，真正的真相是：這個家庭只領過四個月的補助，而那是距今 13 年前的往事。推文讓許多網友群情激憤，然而令他人感到憤怒的狀況，基本上並不存在。

是誰扎了稻草人？為什麼要綁一個，沒有任何烏鴉會停留的稻草人？也許，把視線轉移到他者身上，用憤怒驅動自己前進，就能降低自己生活中觸目可見的不順心。唯獨有些火，燒過了頭，放火的人也是會燙到手的。

《仇恨上線中》電影劇照／劇照提供：公共電視

「千佳先生」在日本法院明令禁止仇恨集會時，忽然停止不發文了。他讓自己跟庫德人仇恨言論保持距離，甚至對鏡頭說：「如果真的有人因為庫德人而受到傷害，那他當然可以出來發表評論⋯⋯但現在看起來，是局外人在搧風點火。」

對庫德人的仇恨從川口發生，散布到全國；如今嚇到的人，竟是最初縱火的人。

歧視是如何鍊成的，臺灣人可一點也不陌生：移花接木的短影片，沒有來由的長文、強渡惡意的立場，戮力曲解某人的言論。要毀掉一個（群）人，首要要讓他們面目可憎，讓眾人產生理由去相信，自己有義務「解決」某個問題，以讓我們的生活「變得更好」。

──然而，這是真的嗎？我們製造了一個敵人，就真的能使我們的生活安然無恙嗎？又或者只是煉成了歧視？《仇恨上線中》給了警世的思考。

【2026 世界公視大展】主視覺。／圖像提供：公共電視

我們正站在一個全新的世界入口。

演算法塑造了我們看見的世界，人工智慧改變了愛與死亡的界線，仇恨與謠言能跨越國界迅速蔓延，而國家權力與科技，也正以前所未有的方式介入我們的記憶、身分與日常生活。這個世界比以往更加便利，也更加複雜；資訊更加自由，真相卻未必更容易抵達。

〈美麗新世界〉並非歌頌一個理想未來，而是邀請觀眾重新想像，我們究竟正在走向哪裡。本屆影展共十四部作品橫跨五個單元，從歷史創傷、女性生命、數位科技、媒體操控，到全球政治與極端化現象，帶領我們穿越看似陌生卻早已降臨的現實，在一次次觀看與思辨之中，共同理解這個正在成形的美麗新世界。

article_text:
The current edition of Amman Design Week focuses on the layers of heritage in the Jordanian capital and demonstrates how the objects around us are never silent.

The Hangar at Ras El Ain was built in the 1930s to house the generators that powered a young and quickly growing Amman, its steel trusses still carrying a faintly ecclesiastical industrial air. It makes an apt and spacious anchor for the fourth Amman Design Week, which returns after seven years away under the theme Accumulations and with the voices of over 220 regional creatives. Their works, by turns fleeting and permanent, drift out of the Hangar to parks, disused street corners and resurrected heritage buildings, and as far as Hellenistic ruins in the valley or at the edge of the Red Sea – activating these civic pockets with design of every temperament, from the plainly useful to the archival, conceptual, experimental, interrogative or devotional.

Much of the work comes from practitioners experimenting well beyond the conventions of their own disciplines; architects thinking as artists and artists taking up the parameters of space and use, or designers treating everyday objects as surfaces for storytelling. Leaving room for such experiment underpins the approach of architect Faysal Tabbarah, this year’s exhibitions’ curator, who has arranged the selection along a sliding scale of design that is “entirely functional, vaguely functional, or provocatively functional”.

The most monumental reach of that scale lies at the edge of the capital in the valley at Iraq Al Amir, where small snails and figs of blown glass have found their way into the ruins of Qasr Al Abd. Settling among the colossal limestone blocks of the Hellenistic palace is the installation Ahl Al Bayt (the ‘People of the House’) (2026) by Dima Srouji, whose practice has long dwelt on archaeology and the ethics of excavation. In Amman, she began with a diary from 1904 describing the abundant waters of the valley and imagined the landscape itself as the palace’s first inhabitant, the life of its springs and creeks returning in glass to a building thought never to have been completed.

Back in the city, Amman’s past in antiquity resurfaces also in Ras El Ain Park, where Civil Architecture’s Folly (2026) threads a canopy of glazed tiles, made with ceramicist Sama El Saket, between the trees. Its roof is scattered with tiny clay figures that look freshly excavated, although the architects describe them playfully rather as ambiguous caryatids. Inside the Hangar, Laith Matarweh and Hanan Salameh’s Al-Mastaba (2026) reverses the gesture with a bench of stone and concrete speculated as a future ruin, with gaps left open for weeds to grow through, as Éditions Levantine reflects on Mesopotamian tablets inscribed with artful cuneiform through a configuration of mirrors in marquetry and reflective steel.

Meanwhile. at Darat Abu Adnan, Faissal El-Malak dresses the iron swirls and diamond-shaped grilles of the rear windows with colour and geometry, which in part appear like an Ionic column rendered in stained glass. Built in the 1950s for the Abu Hassan family and one of the few heritage homes still standing in Jabal Al Lweibdeh, the house has been restored for this edition, its rooms treated as an archive of domestic life. The work installed here answers in kind, with Kinda Ghannoum’s carpets billowing gently in the arched loggia at the entrance, their pixelated motifs carrying a handicraft into a digital visual language, while the hand-carved maamoul moulds of SPOCs for Gaza Design Studio hang by the kitchen. Out in the garden, Farah Tajeddin’s candleholders of Dead Sea salt seem to melt slowly on a rock. “They hold light but also carry the material and memory of a landscape,” she says, adding that the commission drew her to move between utility and sculpture at a more object scale than the experiential scale at which she typically works.

The restoration is one of several ways in which the week means to outlast its 16 days, its organisers describing it as a year-round cultural and creative ecosystem. Folly will remain in Ras El Ain Park long after the event, as will L.E.FT Architects’ Ard Al Sahn (2026), which carries a mosque’s forecourt across the road, turning an overlooked junction into an active public square with stone offcut prayer rugs that double as paving.

For a design week (or two) built around accumulation, these are the works that will keep accruing, gathering wear and the habits of a neighbourhood long after the programme has ended. Tabbarah describes the framework he gave designers as a question of how daily practices, environments and cultural memories “come together, entangle”, and the most legible trace of that thinking sits in the captions, where each work appears beside an archival image chosen by its maker, offered “to suggest that none of our work comes from nothing”. “Everyone’s work is built on an idea, an object, an artefact, a piece of oral history that informs what we do today,” continues Tabbarah. The Hangar is curated to allow that lineage to be felt and interacted with, unfolding loosely from a room that he likens to a material inventory towards a final space given over to the ground and to playful re-narrations of history. He estimates that only around a quarter of what is shown has reached production, the rest presented as prototypes and seed projects, lending the exhibition the character of a working archive, more so than merely a transient showroom of products and objects of design.

Amman Design Week runs until 17 October

article_text:
“It’s the feeling of hearing Stevie Wonder’s ‘Happy Birthday’ song for the first time, or enjoying a film projection of an old movie from a warm jacuzzi while drinking a cold beer. It’s the summer breeze with sparklers, sandy hair, and the smell of fresh flowers in the morning.” That’s how Shelby Duncan describes what the house on Canyon Drive was between 2009 and 2015: less an address than a feeling.

The house itself was real enough: a classic California craftsman tucked beneath the giant white Hollywood sign, not far from Griffith Park, with a big backyard, a vintage pool, a guesthouse, and a garage studio that sheltered a rotating cast of traveling artists over the years. The door, they say, never closed. “The rule number one and biggest privilege in this house was that you were allowed to show up exactly as you are,” Shelby and Saraï sum up. No invitation, no guest list, just that one unspoken clause that held, for six years, for the 500 artists who passed through House of Love .

Shelby Duncan lived those six years camera in hand, day by day. “I never ‘thought’ about taking photos in or for the House of Love,” she confides in the book. “I was capturing the moments that moved me, the bonds and friendships that inspired me, moments of life and of everyday living.” The timing matters. The Canyon Drive years straddled a tipping point: smartphones were finding their way into every pocket, and Instagram (launched in October 2010) was only just beginning to turn every party into a shop window. Shelby, meanwhile, shot on film, with direct flash or available light, and found out what the night had given her once the prints came back from the lab. What happened there was lived first and looked at later. She kept all of it: “I photographed everything in this house. I wanted to live and immortalize every moment.”

What the photographs tell comes closer to a night that never ends. Sparklers and fireworks set off in the backyard, a couple diving fully clothed into a pool ringed with banana trees, watermelons split open by hand for an impromptu shoot, a costume party where a bride in white tulle brushes shoulders with a guest in face paint drinking straight from a jar. On one wall, a mosaic of Polaroids gathers dozens of faces, some anonymous, some not yet famous, all caught in the same half-drunk, half-sincere grin. Elsewhere, in a dim bar, a man holds up a woman tipping backward, hair falling loose, mouth open; the photograph, like so many here, wants nothing more than that particular kind of vertigo.

People fell in love at House of Love as readily as they danced, and it often started in the kitchen. Pantea Ghaderi met both loves of her life there, years apart: “I met both of them in the kitchen years apart from each other, but both changed the course of my life. The first made me a better version of myself and showed me a new way of being and loving. And the second, well he gave me the greatest gift of all, he made me a mother to our twins.” Antoine Debarge sums up that same kitchen more economically: “This kitchen gave me two magical twins, thank you Tefal.” One assumes the pan is still around somewhere. Mégane Quashie found less a lover than herself: “My heart heals within the walls and the hands of people who pass through the House of Love,” she writes, adding that she learned “how to love again, but more importantly how to love myself again.” A secret garden for Melody Ehsani. A lost paradise for Emmanuel Fansten.

Legend has it the music never stopped. Every chapter of the book opens with a playlist put together by Shelby and Saraï: 1950s doo-wop, Woodstock rock, disco funk. Phoenix rehearsed their guitars there before filling the Hollywood Bowl. Matthieu Chedid wrote a song about it, La Maison de Saraï (“Saraï’s House”). One photograph shows Johnny Hallyday from behind, backstage, lighting a cigarette among the amplifiers; having come to dance for a full night, he would later say he hadn’t felt that kind of energy since the seventies, running around with Keith Richards. His wife, Laeticia Hallyday, remembers a freedom rediscovered, a creative period that “became a way of coming back to life,” a light “fragile, intense, and full of gratitude.”

The visiting celebrities weren’t spared the rule either. Louis Garrel and Gaspard Ulliel stepped in front of Shelby’s lens in 2012; others left words behind. For Léa Seydoux, a bubble in which to feel safe, a house that “will stay in my mind forever.” For Rebecca Zlotowski, a scattered memory, “a collection of images, snapshots, fragments of light,” with Saraï’s bathroom forever resurfacing. For Tessa Thompson, a place “where you could be idle while still buzzing with life.” For Jim Sturgess, freshly landed from London, the Los Angeles he’d been looking for all along, “a collective for the strange and the wonderful.” For Cécile Cassel, a dream of weightlessness: “I thought I could fly. See you soon, House of Love…” All it took, to half believe it, was climbing onto the roof.

Jena Malone remembers that roof quite literally. “I remember getting to know Shelby through heartbreaks and rebirths, all the way up to her small room under the eaves. Climbing onto the roof. That roof, I will always remember it.” Even now, she says, driving through the Franklin neighborhood is enough to make her shoulders drop, and to bring back the urge to “go looking for a little trouble and some good conversation.”

The definition Shelby Duncan gives, in the text that opens the book, of whatever kept the house standing for six years: “Love is not always easy. Love is challenging. Love tests us. Love is hard. Love is painful. Love is vulnerable. Love is the opposite of control.” And further on: “We all surprised each other. We all celebrated each other. We all valued each other.” Rock’n’roll, House of Love ? Without a doubt.

Some fifteen years later, the Paris show, following the one in Arles this summer, asks the question in three parts: “What was love yesterday? What is love today? What is love in this very moment?” Yesterday, a kitchen, a roof, a door that was always open. Today, it’s up to each of us to see what’s left of it on our phones. House of Love has found a Paris address worthy of it. Founded in 1949 by Bernard Gheerbrant, between the Café de Flore and Les Deux Magots, La Hune served as a rallying point for Sartre and the existentialists, showed Robert Doisneau as early as 1951 and Picasso in 1957, before becoming YellowKorner’s Paris bookshop-gallery in 2015. Shelby Duncan’s images are on view there from October 14 to November 15, the closing day of Paris Photo.

A coincidence of timing: YellowKorner is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year and has placed it under the banner of joy, partying, love, and togetherness, which is to say the same program as on Canyon Drive. Founded in 2006 to make photography accessible to as many people as possible, the company publishes prints in limited, numbered editions, shown in 80 galleries across more than 20 countries. It also supports artists beyond sales: for “House of Love,” YellowKorner provided some financial backing for the project and produced all of the exhibition’s prints in its own lab, which handles everything from matted, framed prints to large-format fine art.

The book, published by 37.2 Paris on June 12 after four years and 250 testimonies, is its paper trace. The house closed its doors in 2015. Shelby Duncan, who now lives in Paris, may be thinking of giving it a second life in France. Enough to bring back that half-drunk, half-sincere grin lighting up every Polaroid on the wall.

The exhibition “House of Love” by Shelby Duncan is on view at La Hune , in Paris, from October 17 to November 15, 2026. Exhibition opening, open to the public, on November 4, 2026, from 6pm.

Curators: Shelby Duncan, Nicolas Huet Greub – Major partners: 37.2, La Hune, YellowKorner, LabKorner, Everest Photo, Agence PAM, Processus Photo.

The eponymous book is published by 37.2 Paris and available for €70.

article_text:
Opinion

Is Sexy Art Back, or Is It Just Me?

From Willem de Kooning’s miserable nudes to Alexandra Barth’s hot and bothered architecture, sex is in the air in Chicago.

Slow Dance at the MCA Chicago (photo courtesy MCA Chicago)

CHICAGO — I see a lot of exhibitions in Chicago, and lately, I have been noticing more than a few that feel almost ridiculously erotic. I mean, I get it, there's always been plenty of eros in art, but I haven't observed it much lately at the school where I teach nor in the shows that I view. Is sex back? Or it could just be me. I turned 50 this past year, and popular culture suggests that this might be what happens around my age, à la Sharon Horgan's Youth and Olivia Colman's Wicker , both recent screen-based explorations of lusty midlife ladyhood.

For those who have never had one or maybe never will, female middle-age libido sets at either zero or 1,000, on a scale of one to 100. It is not an easy ride. Shifting from one state to the other causes severe whiplash for driver and passengers alike. That’s based on an admittedly minuscule survey, though fear not, this will not be a personal essay about my own sexuality or that of my acquaintances. God, no. Maybe after everyone’s dead. What proceeds, instead, is a round-up of exhibitions that, for me, have a strong connecting thread, obviously red, and not discussed much if at all in the various associated didactics.

Willem de Kooning Drawing at the Art Institute of Chicago (photo Jonathan Mathias, courtesy Art Institute of Chicago)

What shows? Last spring, Alice Tippit ’s sly, meticulous paintings at the DePaul Art Museum had me thinking I probably needed to start talking to a therapist again, because what was going on in my head was not articulated anywhere in the otherwise delightful catalogue. Not even close. During the summer, SHADOW at tête-à-tête-à-tête, a wicked little curatorial project of Shannon Stratton, included Holly Murkerson’s sensuous photographs of a stone passageway worth entering and two dark leather-and-wood stools by David Sprecher and Neiva Mulhearn that required straddling and peering into.

What wasn’t a turn-on was the Art Institute of Chicago’s summer blockbuster, Willem de Kooning Drawing . You wouldn’t know from the glowing reviews or polite museum text that miserable naked women filled the walls. I like a good nude as much as anyone, but at some point, maybe it was the third room — definitely by the time I got to the giant rowboat charcoals of the mid-60s — de Kooning’s subjects started to look like crime victims.

Left: Lee Miller, “Woman with Hand on Head” (also known as “Coiffure”) (1931), photograph; right: Lee Miller, “Charlie Chaplin with chandelier" (1932), photograph (both photos courtesy Art Institute of Chicago)
