article_text:
In a fictional universe of pixel characters and data collectors, the artist’s maximalist materialism underscores a dark reality

For years, Pap Souleye Fall has chronicled themes of overconsumption, digital capture and technological hypervisibility through the exploits of DEAD PIXEL, a character named after the permanently dark dots that sometimes result from screen malfunctions, whose bodily senses were extracted by his nemesis, THE DATA COLLECTOR. Fall’s fictional universe unfolds across exhibitions and performances that weave together recurring visual motifs, aspects of their personal life and references to West African aesthetics and history, particularly those of Senegal, where they were raised before relocating to the United States. When performing as DEAD PIXEL, they don a crudely stitched full-body chroma-key-green garment adorned with imitation pearls. The garment mimics the motion-capture suits used to film visual effects in movies and games. At MIT’s List Center, parts of one of Fall’s suits are sutured into a patchwork of green tattered fabric trailing up a wall. A green arm protrudes from the stitching like an avatar caught in the dimensional breach between digital and physical realms.

In a room-size installation titled NOMANISANISLAND REDIRTRENDER (2026), a ramshackle lattice of giant ‘matchsticks’ – wooden stems tipped with papier-mâché heads – houses found objects and humorous curios tenuously metabolised with c-clamps into the scaffolding alongside past artworks (notably portions of a gargantuan peanut, an agricultural commodity forcibly cultivated during colonial Senegal that became a vital cash crop after independence). Below Fall’s DEAD PIXEL suit is a small figure-eight formed by cowrie shells that resembles both a peanut and an infinity symbol, calling to mind the presumption of limitless growth that fuels capitalist consumption and the history of shell money as legal tender in West Africa. Near Fall’s rickety scaffolding are dozens of ‘books’ composed of richly illustrated wooden blocks that hinge open to reveal pixelated drawings. Many bear enigmatic texts on the legacies of colonial power: ‘EMPIRE RISE; EMPIRE FALL’, reads one; ‘INVISIBLE TO WHOM’, reads another. These codices nod to the speculative worldbuilding of comics and manga, which often allow readers to project power fantasies, contend with historical trauma and imagine better alternatives.

Fall’s installation gives presence and vitality to scrapped objects, invisible digital infrastructures and subjugated histories of colonialism, war and enslavement. Found everyday materials are transformed with playfulness and glee: an inflatable Santa dressed in military camouflage is repapered in blue, lime and forest-green swatches; a dollhouse atop the structure is layered in spandex; the structure’s multicoloured wooden beams appear held together by tape. Despite all the wit and whimsy, Fall’s maximalist materialism underscores a dark reality: that capitalism’s seemingly immaterial digital infrastructures yield tangible waste. Fortunately, it is possible for discarded digital media to be inscribed with new meanings; see, for example, the elaborate pixel-art drawings Fall scratched into screens recovered from e-waste sites. These etchings depict the variations on the recurring iconography of their saga, including the palm trees of Senegal, the peanut and DEAD PIXEL posing with limbs outstretched, reunited with body parts symbolising the senses captured by THE DATA COLLECTOR. At a time when digital systems promise seamless immersive experiences, the work here reminds us that imagining a world beyond totalising structures of capture is perhaps a matter of embracing the glitches in these systems, where the seams between lived reality, digital simulation and speculative worldbuilding begin to fray.

List Projects 35: Pap Souleye Fall at MIT List Visual Arts Center, Cambridge, 30 July – 29 November

title_original: 週末いきたい！ 11月14日はモネの誕生日！モネ・印象派の魅力に浸れる展覧会をピックアップしました
editorial_title_zh: 周末想去！11月14日是莫奈的生日！我们挑选了能沉浸于莫奈与印象派魅力的展览
editorial_excerpt_zh: 11月14日是印象派巨匠克劳德·莫奈的第186个生日。在这个值得纪念的时刻，我们挑选了非常值得一看的展览。莫奈作品与当代艺术的对话、与莫奈并肩齐驱的巨匠、印象派及其前后画家的“联系”等，不妨从各种视角深入领略印象派与莫奈的魅力吧。

article_text:
11月14日は、印象派の巨匠クロード・モネの186回目の誕生日です。この記念すべきタイミングに、ぜひ見たい展覧会をピックアップしました。モネの作品と現代アートの対話、モネと肩を並べた巨匠、印象派とその前後の画家の”つながり”など、様々な視点から印象派やモネの魅力を深掘りしてみませんか。

「あたらしい目—モネと21世紀のアート」箱根・ポーラ美術館で2027年4月7日まで モネと現代美術が織りなす濃密な対話

◇11月14日はモネの誕生日！ポーラ美術館で4つのプログラムを開催

「オルセー美術館所蔵 いまを生きる歓び」東京都美術館で11月14日から 「印象派の殿堂」から至宝約110点が集結

「ゴッホの跳ね橋と印象派の画家たち ヴァルラフ=リヒャルツ美術館所蔵」愛知・名古屋市美術館で11月29日まで

印象派を中心にモダン・アートへの道のりを一望する

「わたしたちのルノワール 日本が愛した、幸せの画家」静岡市美術館で11月15日まで 国内所蔵のルノワール作品39点が一堂に集結 モネやセザンヌなどフランス近代美術の巨匠の作品も

「フランス近代絵画の祝宴」岐阜県美術館で12月13日まで 笠間日動美術館と岐阜県美術館のコレクションによる夢の共演、巨匠たちの名品200点超が一堂に

あわせて読みたい

【関西文化の日】2府8県で美術館・博物館・資料館などが入館無料に！2026年のメインは11月14日～15日です

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班）
